newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rate rise to help C/A, may up zloty-Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Polish rate rise to help C/A, may up zloty-Salomon.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's official rate rise on Monday is likely to help stop the widening of the country's current account deficit and may give the zloty a slight boost, analysts at Salomon Brothers in London said.

The NBP raised its two main rates, the lombard and discount rates, by two and 2.5 points respectively to 27 and 24.5 percent respectively to dampen credit growth and decrease imports to curb the widening of Poland's current account gap.
The current account deficit rose to $2.4 billion in the January-May period of this year against $345 million in the same period of 1996.

"The rate hike will modestly raise borrowing costs and thus will help to slow domestic demand growth, which is running at a high seven percent year-on-year pace, and help to break the trend in the balance of payments," they wrote in a report.
"The impact on the zloty is probably neutral to mildly positive," the Salomon Brothers report said.
On Monday the zloty gained half a percentage point against the basket of currencies on domestic buying supported by the central bank rate rise.
Salomon Brothers' analysts said however that the zloty would stand a better chance of gains if the central bank's rate rise was followed by a rise in Treasury bill yields.
"Although some increase in T-bill yields is probable, it is not certain," they said.

The report said changes in the zloty's crawling devaluation mechanism of one percent a month were unlikely until the end of the year while its 1998 prospects depended on the policies of Poland's new parliament after the September 21 elections.
